name: Madang
note: Town: provincial capital and main base on the Madang north-coast harbour; Wikivoyage's start point for the coast.

name: Madang Central Market
note: Market: busy local market in the centre of Madang, open daily, with produce brought in from the Highlands.

name: Coastwatchers Lighthouse
note: Landmark: working lighthouse on Madang harbour, a memorial to the WWII coastwatchers.

name: Madang Museum
note: Museum: small natural-science and ethnographic museum in Madang, sharing a building with the visitor bureau (Wikipedia cites Lonely Planet).

name: Krangket Island
note: Island: five-minute boat trip from Madang; two villages with gardens, a lagoon beach and a basic lodge.

name: Siar Island
note: Island: quiet island near Krangket, grouped with it in a travel guide for swimming, diving and picnics.

name: Samun Island
note: Island: quiet island near Madang named with Krangket and Siar in a travel guide; no detail in the source.

name: Bagabag Island
note: Island: reef island near Karkar; a travel listing warns of strong currents over its reefs; no visitor infrastructure in the sources.

name: Karkar Island
note: Island: volcanic island 30 km off Madang with a caldera volcano (last big eruptions 1974-75), a ring road and views back to Madang; known for bilums.

name: Karkar Bilum Festival
note: Festival: annual bilum-weaving festival on Karkar Island (October or November); an event, not a permanent spot.

name: Madang Festival
note: Festival: annual Madang festival on the June long weekend, with sing-sings; an event, not a permanent spot.

name: Balek Wildlife Sanctuary
note: Nature: village wildlife sanctuary about 30 minutes from Madang, where a sulphur creek runs through a limestone cave to a clear stream with turtles and eels; tours via Melanesian Tourist Services.

name: Bil Bil Village
coordinates_source: osm:place/islet Bil Bil Island (village point, name match)
note: Village: quiet village reached by tour from Madang (the source's text on it is cut off, so the draw is unconfirmed).

name: Hobe Village
note: Village: village stay about 30 minutes by minibus from Madang, with birdwatching and WWII Japanese hideouts.

name: Haya Village
note: Village: village guesthouse near Madang offering village stays and birdwatching.

name: Madang Japanese WWII Airfield
note: WWII relic site: overgrown Japanese airfield on the north coast with plane wrecks, bomb craters and a large Mitsubishi 'Betty' bomber; half-day tour (Wikivoyage).

name: Tupira Surf Club
note: Surf break: surf club about 90 minutes up the coast from Madang; hosted a World Longboard Championships.

name: Mitchell Bomber Wreck (Madang)
note: Dive site: WWII B-25 Mitchell bomber wreck near Madang, largely intact, a shallow wreck dive.

name: Planet Rock
note: Dive site: submerged pinnacle a short boat ride from Madang, with strong currents and sharks. Title is a disambiguation; no Wikipedia article for the dive site, so 0 views.

name: Magic Passage
note: Dive site: narrow drift-dive passage about five minutes by boat from Madang Resort, with coral gardens and garden eels.

name: USS Boston Wreck
note: Wreck dive: US Navy minesweeper (converted Liberty ship) sunk on a reef drop-off off Madang, about 30 m deep.

name: Coral Queen Wreck
note: Wreck dive: wreck known for a night dive when flashlight fish leave its holds at sunset.

name: Babang Island
note: Island: remote dive island on a submerged mountain chain, with fringing reefs and sea-mounts; reached by liveaboard.

name: Purdy Islands
note: Islands: remote dive islands offshore from Madang, reached by liveaboard only. Wikipedia pin lies at 2.9S, far off this coast; no point taken.

name: Hansa Bay
note: Bay: WWII Japanese naval base on the north coast between Madang and Wewak; a travel guide cites sunken warships in Hansa and Bogia bays for diving.

name: Bogia
note: Town: district centre on the north coast between Madang and Wewak; Bogia Bay has sunken warships cited for diving in a travel guide.

name: Astrolabe Bay
note: Bay: large bay of the Bismarck Sea off Madang's coast, the water Madang looks onto; no separate visitor draw in the sources.

name: Saidor
note: Village: Rai Coast district centre and site of the 1944 Saidor landing (WWII); no visitor source names a draw.

name: Adelbert Range
note: Mountain range: rainforest range behind Madang (highest point 1,716 m) with bird-of-paradise habitat; no visitor source names a route.

name: Sio
note: Village: north-coast village on the Huon Peninsula where Japanese forces were pushed out in 1943-44 (WWII); no visitor source names a draw.

name: Lae
note: Town: PNG's second city and Morobe's capital, at the start of the Highlands Highway; gateway to the Highlands and Huon Gulf.

name: Lae Botanic Gardens
note: Gardens: city gardens in central Lae with PNG plants, birds and an old aeroplane; not always open to the public (Wikipedia).

name: Lae War Cemetery
note: Cemetery: Commonwealth war cemetery with about 2,800 WWII burials, next to the botanic gardens and including the Lae Memorial.

name: Rainforest Habitat
note: Wildlife: 10-hectare animal and bird display at Lae University of Technology, with about 80 birds of paradise in a rainforest enclosure.

name: Morobe Show
note: Event: annual agricultural and cultural show held on the weekend nearest the October full moon; an event, not a permanent spot.

name: Lae Game Fishing
note: Activity: game-fishing charters (marlin, sailfish, wahoo, yellowfin) arranged through the Lae Yacht Club; an operator-based activity.

name: Lae Main Market
note: Market: Lae's main food market, described in Wikipedia as the best food market in PNG; trading days not stated in the source.

name: Mount Lunaman
note: Hill: 96 m hill in central Lae (Hospital Hill), with WWII Japanese tunnels; public access not stated in the source.

name: Huon Peninsula
note: Peninsula: large rugged peninsula of north-east Morobe with WWII Huon campaign sites, the Finisterre and Saruwaged ranges; region-scale, not a single base.

name: Finschhafen
note: Town: Huon Peninsula town 80 km east of Lae, a WWII US naval base and early Lutheran mission; reached by a weekly ship from Lae (Wikivoyage PNG).

name: Tami Islands
note: Islands: small island group 13 km from Finschhafen, known for wooden bowls, carvings and masks; no visitor source names access.

name: Umboi Island
note: Island: volcanic island in the Siassi group between Huon Peninsula and New Britain; a weekly ship from Lae stops there (Wikivoyage PNG).

name: Siassi Islands
note: Island group: 18 islands (7 inhabited) of the Siassi group, known for traditional trade; a region-level grouping with no visitor source.

name: Sakar Island
note: Volcano: stratovolcano island in the Bismarck Sea with a summit crater lake; no recorded eruptions; no visitor source.

name: Black Cat Track
note: Trail: rough 3-4 day overland trek from Salamaua to Wau, a gold-rush and WWII route now used by experienced trekkers.

name: Salamaua
note: Village: former port on the Huon Gulf, starting point of the Black Cat Track, with WWII Japanese base ruins (Wikipedia); reached by boat from Lae.

name: Wau
note: Town: gold-rush town at about 1,100 m, the Black Cat Track's inland end, with the Wau Ecology Institute nearby.

name: Wau Ecology Institute
note: Research station: biological field station near Wau (since 1961) with research collections; visitor access not stated in the sources.

name: Bulolo
note: Town: former gold-dredging town on the Bulolo River, 32 km north-west of Wau, with dredge relics and a golf course.

name: Bulolo Gold Dredges
note: Relic: eight 2,000-tonne gold dredges airlifted into the Bulolo valley; some abandoned in the valley and still visible (Wikivoyage).

name: Bulolo Golf Course
note: Activity: PNG's oldest golf course, a nine-hole course opened in 1947 (Wikivoyage); a sport venue, not a sight.

name: Aseki and Watama
coordinates_source: osm:place/town Aseki (nearest named place; Watama not in OSM)
note: Villages: Anga villages about 100 km south-west of Bulolo, famous for traditional smoked burials; remote, needs a guide.

name: Herzog Mountains
note: Mountain range: range about 22 km west of Lae with Mount Herzog (1,389 m); no visitor source names a route.

name: Finisterre Range
note: Mountain range: north-eastern PNG range with the WWII Battle of Shaggy Ridge; highest point Mount Boising; trekking and mountaineering.

name: Mount Boising
note: Peak: highest point of the Finisterre Range (unofficial name), first climbed in 2014; mountaineering only.

name: Saruwaged Range
note: Mountain range: Huon Peninsula range dominated by the Sarawaget Massif (Mount Bangeta); trekking and mountaineering.

name: YUS Conservation Area
note: Conservation area: about 760 km2 in the northern Huon Peninsula, habitat of the endangered Matschie's tree-kangaroo; no visitor infrastructure in the sources.

name: Sattelberg
note: Village: village on a 900 m peak above Finschhafen, the site of the 1943 Sattelberg battle (WWII); no visitor source names a draw.

name: Siki Cove
note: Cove: 1943 Allied landing site near Finschhafen (WWII); no visitor source names a draw.

name: Dreger Harbour
note: Harbour: WWII US Navy PT-boat base and Seabee camp near Finschhafen; no visitor source names a draw.

name: Mort Bay
note: Bay: named after a US Navy commander of WWII; stub article, no visitor source names a draw.

name: Mageri Point
note: Peninsula: headland in Morobe; stub article, no visitor source names a draw.

name: MV Rabaul Queen Wreck
note: Wreck: passenger ferry that sank in 2012 about 16 km off Finschhafen with heavy loss of life; no public access in the sources.
